## Full Workflow — Step by Step

### Phase 1: Research & Training Data
```
1. Scrape 1 hour of viral animation content from Instagram/TikTok
   - Focus: stickman, vector, 2D animation styles going viral
   - Save as video files or screenshots

2. Feed content to Claude:
   "Analyze these viral animations. Identify: movement style,
   character proportions, scene pacing, transition types,
   color palette, what makes them shareable."

3. Claude outputs: animation style guide + viral pattern breakdown
```

### Phase 2: Script
```
4. Give Claude your documentary topic / story

5. Prompt:
   "Write a 60-second animated script for [TOPIC].
   Format: scene-by-scene with character actions, dialogue,
   and visual descriptions. Style: punchy, fast-paced,
   stickman animation format. Hook in first 3 seconds."

6. Revise 2–3 times until tight
```

### Phase 3: Character Design Sheets
```
7. Prompt Claude (or GPT Plus for higher quality):
   "Create a character design sheet for [CHARACTER].
   Style: simple stickman vector. Include:
   - Default standing pose
   - Walking cycle frames (8 frames)
   - Talking pose
   - Reaction poses (surprised, thinking, pointing)
   - Side view + front view
   Output as SVG code."

8. Save character sheets as SVG files
9. These become reusable across ALL future animations
```

### Phase 4: Background Generation
```
10. Prompt Claude/GPT:
    "Generate a [SCENE TYPE] background as SVG.
    Style: flat vector, minimal, stickman-compatible.
    Scene: [office / street / dark room / forest / courtroom]
    Color palette: [YOUR CHANNEL COLORS]"

11. Build a background library — reuse across episodes
    Common backgrounds needed:
    - News desk / interview room
    - Street / outdoor
    - Office / corporate
    - Dark room (crime/conspiracy)
    - Historical setting
```

### Phase 5: Animation Code (The Core)
```
12. Feed Claude:
    - The script
    - Character SVGs
    - Background SVGs
    - Style reference from Phase 1

13. Master prompt (see section below)

14. Claude outputs: complete HTML/CSS/JS animation file
    - Characters move on screen
    - Scene transitions built in
    - Timing synced to script beats
    - Runs in browser

15. Revise in 2–3 rounds:
    Round 1: Get rough version working
    Round 2: Fix timing and movement
    Round 3: Polish transitions and pacing
```

### Phase 6: Voiceover
```
Budget:  Claude generates TTS voiceover
Quality: ElevenLabs — pick voice matching your doc's tone

16. Feed final script to voice tool
17. Export as MP3/WAV
18. Time voiceover to animation beats
```

### Phase 7: Sound Effects
```
19. Sources (all free):
    - Freesound.org
    - Mixkit.co/free-sound-effects
    - Pixabay.com/sound-effects
    - Zapsplat.com

20. SFX needed for stickman animations:
    - Footstep sounds (walking scenes)
    - Whoosh (transitions)
    - Impact sounds (action beats)
    - Ambient background (scene-setting)
    - Notification/alert pings
```

### Phase 8: Final Assembly
```
21. CapCut (free):
    - Import: rendered animation video + voiceover + SFX
    - Layer audio tracks
    - Sync SFX to visual events
    - Add title cards (GPT Plus generated)
    - Export 1080p or 4K

22. Alternatively: ffmpeg-skill
    - Claude watches the assembled video
    - Adjusts audio levels automatically
    - Normalizes to -14 LUFS YouTube standard
    - Final export optimized
```

## The Master Prompt (Animation Code)

```
You are an expert web animator. Create a complete, self-contained HTML file
that renders the following stickman animation:

SCRIPT: [PASTE YOUR SCRIPT]

CHARACTER DESIGNS: [PASTE SVG CHARACTER SHEETS]

BACKGROUNDS: [PASTE SVG BACKGROUNDS]

REQUIREMENTS:
- Pure HTML/CSS/JS — no external libraries
- 60 seconds total duration
- Characters animate smoothly (use CSS keyframes or requestAnimationFrame)
- Scene transitions: [fade / slide / cut]
- Sync character movement to script beats
- Include: walking cycles, talking animations, reaction poses
- Color palette: [YOUR COLORS]
- Canvas size: 1920x1080 (16:9)
- Export-ready: animation plays automatically on load

OUTPUT: Single complete HTML file that plays the full animation.
```

---

## Claude Revision Prompts

### Round 1 — Get It Working
> "Run this and tell me what's broken. Fix any errors and make the animation play start to finish without stopping."

### Round 2 — Timing
> "The [CHARACTER] walks too slowly at [TIMESTAMP]. The transition at [SCENE] is too abrupt. Speed up the walking animation by 40% and add a 0.3s fade between scenes 2 and 3."

### Round 3 — Polish
> "Add these finishing touches:
> 1. Subtle bounce to character idle animation
> 2. Background parallax effect on scene 4
> 3. Text captions matching the voiceover timing
> 4. Smooth ease-in-out on all movements (no linear animations)"

## Rendering Your HTML ? Video

### Method 1: Browser + Screen Record
```
1. Open HTML file in Chrome (full screen)
2. Record with OBS (free) at 1080p60
3. Export recording
```

### Method 2: Puppeteer (Automated)
```javascript
// Have Claude write this script for you
const puppeteer = require('puppeteer');
// Launches browser, plays animation, records frames, stitches to MP4
```

### Method 3: ffmpeg-skill
```
"Watch this animation HTML file rendered as video.
Export as MP4 optimized for YouTube Shorts (1080x1920 vertical)
with audio track attached."
```
